correctness.rationale: For arbitrary six vertices, 36 R_g^2=C1+C2+D from centroid pair distances; summing three four-point parallelogram identities gives 4 sum_{i<j} |M_i-M_j|^2=C1+C2-2D. Thus R_g^2=(C1+C2)/24-(1/18) sum |M_i-M_j|^2. Under all six unit edges and equal bond angle theta, 0<theta<2pi/3, C1=6, C2=24 sin^2(theta/2), yielding the claimed sharp bound and exact deficit. Equality requires all opposite-chord midpoints to coincide. The centrally symmetric chair a,b,c,-a,-b,-c is feasible because its forced Gram matrix has strictly positive eigenvalues z/2,z/2,(3-z)/4 for z=4sin^2(theta/2)∈(0,3); equal Gram matrices force congruence even allowing reflection. At arccos(-1/3) this is 11/12. Independent random-coordinate validation on 500 six-tuples corroborated the exact universal identity. The proof does not require self-avoiding or energy-minimizing polygons; endpoints excluded.
